title: All Orders of Different Letters

concept.title: Fill the positions one by one with letters not used yet
body: A **permutation** is an arrangement of all the letters in some order. Fill the positions from left to right. For each position try **every letter that has not been used yet**. A boolean array `used` remembers which letters are already placed. When all positions are filled, one permutation is complete.

If the letters are tried in alphabetical order, the permutations come out in **dictionary order** with no sorting at the end. There are `n!` permutations: 5040 for 7 letters, which is why the word is short.

statement: You are given a word of `n` different lowercase letters (in any order). Print all permutations of its letters, one per line, in dictionary order.
inputFormat: The only line has the word.
outputFormat: The `n!` permutations in dictionary order, one per line.

examples.output:
abc
acb
bac
bca
cab
cba
examples.note: The six permutations in dictionary order are abc, acb, bac, bca, cab and cba.

hints: Sort the letters first, then fill the positions from left to right.
Mark a letter as used when you place it and free it again after the recursive call.
When the arrangement has n letters, record it.

explanation: The letters are sorted, then each position tries every unused letter in order. A letter is marked used while it is placed and freed afterwards, so all `n!` arrangements are produced in dictionary order.
solution.complexity: Time O(n! * n), space O(n) besides the output.

code.python:
def permute(letters, used, current, out):
    if len(current) == len(letters):
        out.append("".join(current))
        return
    for i in range(len(letters)):
        if not used[i]:
            used[i] = True
            current.append(letters[i])
            permute(letters, used, current, out)
            current.pop()
            used[i] = False

word = input().strip()

out = []
permute(sorted(word), [False] * len(word), [], out)
print("\n".join(out))
